what_its_for: Tbo-filgrastim helps your body make more white blood cells called neutrophils. These cells fight infection. This medicine is used to lower your risk of getting a serious infection after you receive certain chemotherapy treatments for cancer. It works by telling your bone marrow (the spongy tissue inside your bones) to produce more infection-fighting white blood cells faster.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in the stomach area, the front of your thighs, or the upper outer area of your arms. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give yourself the injection at home. Always use a new needle and syringe each time. Do not shake the vial or prefilled syringe. Check the liquid before each use — it should be clear and colorless. Do not use it if it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it. Rotate injection sites so you do not inject in the same spot every time.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body weight and your medical condition. The usual dose is given once a day, starting about 24 hours after your chemotherapy session ends. Do not start this medicine within 24 hours before or after receiving chemotherapy. Continue taking it for as many days as your doctor prescribes, even if you feel fine. Your doctor will do blood tests to check your white blood cell counts and decide when to stop.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure what to do.
storage: Store tbo-filgrastim in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it. If it accidentally freezes, throw it away. You may take it out of the refrigerator and keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 5 days. After 5 days at room temperature, throw it away even if there is medicine left. Keep it out of the reach of children. Dispose of used needles and syringes in a proper sharps container — never in your regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive this medicine within 24 hours before or after chemotherapy. Avoid shaking the vial or syringe, as this can damage the medicine. Do not use the medicine if it has been frozen. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are bruised, red, tender, hard, or scarred. Do not reuse needles or syringes. Avoid activities that could cause injury, as this medicine may rarely cause your spleen to enlarge, making it more fragile.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: sudden or severe pain in your upper left belly (abdomen) or left shoulder (this could mean a spleen problem); difficulty breathing, chest pain, or rapid heartbeat; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or feeling faint; bone or muscle pain that is severe and not relieved by over-the-counter pain medicines; signs of infection such as fever over 100.4°F (38°C), chills, or burning with urination; unusual bleeding or bruising; or pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site that does not go away.
when_it_works: Tbo-filgrastim starts working within 1 to 2 days, and your white blood cell counts usually begin to rise within a few days of starting treatment. Blood tests done by your doctor will confirm that the medicine is working. Most people complete their course of treatment within 1 to 2 weeks after each chemotherapy cycle, depending on how quickly their white blood cell counts recover.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Let your doctor know if you have sickle cell disease, as this medicine may cause a serious crisis in people with that condition. Patients with kidney or liver problems should also inform their doctor before starting this medicine. This medicine has been used in children, but dosing may be different — follow your doctor's specific instructions carefully.
